title: Conditional access tagging and workspace snapshot prototype
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Design a compact, scannable UX for understanding who had what access in a workspace at a specific point in time, with the ability to tag access changes as cost-relevant (for chargeback) and to attach conditional rules (time-limited, emergency, delegated).

Problem: Existing audit timelines are noisy and siloed — product teams need a way to: 1) capture a reproducible workspace "snapshot" that includes roles, service accounts, and recent access grants; 2) annotate individual grants with tags (e.g., billable-workload, oncall, third-party) and expiration metadata; 3) quickly escalate or revoke a tag across multiple users; and 4) correlate tagged events with cost and rollout dashboards.

Proposed solution: A two-pane prototype: left pane shows a compact, collapsible chronology of role changes with inline tags and filters; right pane shows a generated workspace snapshot (JSON-lite view + human readable summary) and quick actions (revoke, extend, convert to recurring role, assign to group). Key interactions include: conditional-tag creation (authors can attach rule predicates like "only during PagerDuty oncall window"), bulk-tag apply (select multiple events and apply a tag), snapshot export (to confluence/incident playbook), and cross-linking to cost view (jump-to cost-explorer with pre-applied tag filter).

Design constraints: must fit existing Console header chrome; align with RBAC taxonomy (workspace roles / cross-workspace roles distinction); respect audit log retention policy (older than retention period should show read-only snapshot); and minimize additional permission surface (only users with "audit-write" can tag).

Success metrics: reduced time-to-find access-change root cause by 40% in usability tests; 80% of oncall users can tag and export a snapshot within two clicks in moderated testing.
acceptance_criteria: Prototype demonstrates left-pane timeline with collapsible day buckets and per-event tag chips
Right-pane workspace snapshot renders roles, service accounts, and active conditional rules, and supports export to markdown/Confluence
Tagging flow allows creation of a tag with a predicate (time window or policy name) and attach to multiple events
Quick actions: revoke, extend, convert-to-recurring, and bulk-reassign are present and wired to mocked API responses
Users without audit-write role see tags but cannot create/modify them (visual affordance: disabled action + tooltip)
Clicking a tag can navigate to the console cost explorer with the tag pre-applied (mock link)

decisions: Keep timeline compact by default; expand-on-hover for details to reduce vertical noise
Tags are first-class entities stored in audit metadata (not ephemeral UI labels) to enable cross-product filtering
Export formats: Markdown (for Confluence), JSON-lite (for incident reconstruction), and CSV (for billing teams)
Permissions: only users with 'audit-write' OR 'security-admin' can create/modify tags; others see read-only chips
Cost linking: tags will create soft-anchors to cost-explorer (no tight coupling in MVP)
